title: You’re exhausted…
paragraphs:
You’re exhausted…
but you don’t know how to stop.

Because if you drop it—
who will carry them?

So you keep going.
Holding together people who are falling apart.
Fixing what you didn’t break.
Paying for what you didn’t spend.
Crying in private… while smiling in public.
And everyone calls you “strong.”
But strength is not the same as surrender.

Galatians 6:2 says,
“Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.”
Yes—carry.

But not everything.
Not everyone’s choices.
Not their disobedience dressed as your responsibility.

Because just a few verses later, Scripture balances it:
“For each one should carry their own load.” (Galatians 6:5)
Did you catch that?
There is a difference between a burden and a load.

A burden is crushing—unexpected, overwhelming, beyond capacity.
A load is personal—assigned, owned, accountable before God.

And somewhere along the way…
you started carrying both.
You picked up what God never gave you.

Their addiction.
Their attitude.
Their refusal to change.
Their consequences.
And now your soul is tired in places sleep cannot fix.
But here’s the truth we don’t say enough:

You are not the Holy Spirit.
You are not the Savior.
You are not the fixer of every broken story.
Jesus already took that role—fully, finally, and perfectly.

1 Peter 5:7 says,
“Cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you.”

Not manage it.
Not redistribute it.
Not hide it.
Cast it.
Throw it back to the One strong enough to carry it.

Because when you try to be everyone’s answer,
you slowly forget who your Answer is.

And that’s where burnout begins—
not just in your body, but in your spirit.

You start resenting the very people you’re trying to help.
You feel trapped by love that has turned into obligation.
You begin to serve without joy…
give without grace…
stay without peace.
But here’s what we miss…
Jesus never healed people by becoming enslaved to them.

He loved deeply—
but He also walked away when needed (Luke 5:16).
He served fully—
but He set boundaries clearly (Mark 1:35–38).
He carried the cross—
but only the one assigned by the Father (John 19:17).
Even Jesus did not carry what wasn’t His to carry.
So why are you?

Maybe because saying “no” feels like betrayal.
Maybe because you’ve been taught that sacrifice means silence.
Maybe because you fear that if you stop holding everything together…
everything will fall apart.
But listen carefully:

If your obedience to people is costing your obedience to God,
something is out of order.
You cannot pour from a soul that is spiritually dehydrated.
You cannot rescue others while ignoring your own need for rescue.
And you cannot replace Christ in someone else’s life without losing intimacy with Him in yours.

Matthew 11:28–30—Jesus says:
“Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest… For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”

If what you’re carrying is crushing you…
it didn’t come from Him.
Let that settle.
God will never assign you a weight that replaces your dependence on Him.
So what do you do now?
You return what isn’t yours.

In prayer.
In surrender.
In quiet honesty.
“Lord, this is too heavy for me… because it was never mine to begin with.”
And then you trust Him to do what only He can do.

Convict.
Change.
Restore.
Heal.
Not you.
Him.

Because the Gospel is not just that Jesus saves sinners—
it’s that He frees the weary from playing savior.

On the cross, He didn’t say, “Help Me finish this.”
He said, “It is finished.” (John 19:30)
That includes the weight you’ve been secretly carrying.
So breathe.
Release it.

Not because you don’t care—
but because He cares more than you ever could.
And His hands are stronger than yours.
